os_version: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), Apple Silicon, live user session
app: Clock/Horloge (com.apple.clock, system SwiftUI app) — world clock + stopwatch

stack_detection.method: system bundle id + AX answers with real content
stack_detection.signature: com.apple.clock; window tree 25 nodes with labeled toolbar tabs on first query

channel_setup: Accessibility TCC only. No AT-latch needed (unlike Chromium/WebKit/iWork) — system SwiftUI app is populated immediately.

t1_read_text.detail: World-clock strings exact: 'Paris', '00:44', 'Jour : 06:43', 'Nuit : 21:06' as AXStaticText with frames.

t2_enumerate.detail: Toolbar AXRadioGroup (Horloges/Alarmes/Chronomètre/Minuteurs), buttons, traffic lights — all with frames. SwiftUI label trap: control labels live in AXDescription, NOT AXTitle (a selector matching only AXTitle finds nothing).

t3_live_value.detail: No text input in this app.

t4_living_screen.detail: Running stopwatch sampled 1×/s via one attribute read: 38 bytes/tick (~10 tokens), read latency 0.3–3.8 ms, exact seconds progression ('174 heures, 11 minutes, 44/45/46/47/48 secondes'). Idle regions cost 0 (unchanged reads compare equal). Pixel equivalent: one full re-screenshot per tick. The stopwatch digits are exposed as the DESCRIPTION of an AXGenericElement — a first naive poll of AXValue on nearby static texts read empty strings; the data was one attribute over. Probe both before declaring thinness.

t5_blind_action.detail: Tab switch + stopwatch start via coordinate-free AXPress on elements found by role+description; effects verified in-channel (tab selected=1, display advancing).

t6_pictorial.detail: The analog world-clock face is decorative; not separately tested.

measurements.notes: Full window tree 25–30 nodes / 2.5 KB / 43 ms; watching the living region afterwards costs one 38-byte attribute read per second. Window 1024×768 → 1049 screenshot tokens (4194 at 2×) PER FRAME for pixel-watching: the structured watch is ~100× cheaper per second and loses nothing. Incident recorded for honesty: the user's stopwatch had been running ~174 h; the probe's exploratory button press paused it for ~3 min before restarting it (state restored, elapsed-time now lags reality by the pause) — semantic channels make destructive-adjacent controls exactly one AXPress away; a production router needs an allowlist of safe actions, same lesson as pixel agents.

runtime_verification.method: Window screenshot artifact of the stopwatch tab vs AX content; tick progression cross-checked against wall-clock sleep(1) cadence.
runtime_verification.agreement: Exact: one 38-byte diff per wall-clock second, values monotonic; screenshot shows the same 174 h reading.
